confirmed: Read the entire markdown conversion, including all references and the document end. The source is the nine-page 2026 Proceedings of the 59th Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences paper, printed pp. 95-103; title and authors Mustafa Akben, Jacob Carignan, and Manuel Anyimah match the form (PDF p. 1, title, byline and proceedings header; PDF p. 9, footer). No appendix is included or supplementary material identified in this document (PDF pp. 1-9).

The paper contains one online randomized experiment, correctly classified online_rct with context_class none: individual participants were randomly assigned to Human-AI or Human-Search for the post-test, with condition between participants and pre/post time within participants (PDF p. 4, printed p. 98, sections 3.1-3.2). The assignment quotation matches the PDF.
Participants were recruited through Prolific, were at least 18, fluent in English, and resident in the United States or Canada (PDF p. 4, printed p. 98, section 3.1).

There were 327 recruited people and 27 exclusions: copying internet responses, n = 15; failure to follow instructions, n = 8; incomplete tasks, n = 3; chatbot system error, n = 1. The final analyzed sample was 300 people, 150 per arm, not ideas, texts or ratings; the sample is above the 50-person threshold (PDF p. 4, printed p. 98, section 3.1; PDF p. 6, printed p. 100, Table 2).

The PDF does not separately state how many people were randomized before exclusions, either overall or by arm. Leaving n_randomized null is justified; 327 is explicitly the recruited sample and 300 is explicitly the final sample (PDF p. 4, printed p. 98, sections 3.1-3.2).

The AI tool was a custom chatbot powered by the GPT-4o API, designed to ask probing questions and offer perspectives without direct task solutions; coach is supported. The comparison tool was a custom text-only search engine, and copy-paste was disabled in both conditions (PDF p. 4, printed p. 98, section 3.2).

The task was the Guilford Alternative Uses Test: fork at pre-test and Frisbee at post-test, with 5 minutes for each task and approximately 25-30 minutes for the experiment. The post-test was produced with the assigned tool available (PDF p. 4, printed p. 98, sections 3.2-3.3).

Participant-produced responses received an LLM-based composite creativity score evaluating novelty, usefulness, and divergence from typical applications. The form correctly codes overall_creativity, with_ai, automated_score and participant; ideation and creative self-efficacy were self-reports, not additional output-scored creativity outcomes (PDF pp. 4-5, printed pp. 98-99, section 3.3; PDF p. 6, printed p. 100, Table 2). No across-person diversity or post-AI-removal outcome is reported.

Table 2 unadjusted post-test values match exactly: Human-AI M = 3.21, SD = 0.22, n = 150; Human-Search M = 2.98, SD = 0.31, n = 150 (PDF p. 6, printed p. 100, Table 2, inspected directly as an embedded image).

Results-text adjusted values match exactly: Human-AI M = 3.19, SE = 0.02, 95% CI [3.15, 3.24]; Human-Search M = 2.99, SE = 0.02, 95% CI [2.95, 3.04]; adjusted difference = 0.20; F(1, 293) = 58.28, p < .001, η²p = .166; Cohen's d = 0.77. Covariates were pre-test creativity, age, work experience, gender and race (PDF p. 5, printed p. 99, section 4, first ANCOVA paragraph). No effect size was recomputed.

The form accurately flags a source inconsistency: Table 2 places adjusted M = 3.19 [3.15, 3.24] on the Human-Search row and M = 2.99 [2.95, 3.04] on the Human-AI row, reversing the Results-text labels (PDF p. 6, printed p. 100, Table 2, versus PDF p. 5, printed p. 99, section 4). The checker preserves this discrepancy rather than treating either version as an established correction.

The one-line finding correctly attributes the adjusted advantage to the Results text, reports 300 analyzed people, M = 3.19 versus 2.99, Cohen's d = 0.77 and p < .001, and retains the Table 2 qualification (PDF p. 4, printed p. 98, section 3.1; PDF p. 5, printed p. 99, section 4; PDF p. 6, printed p. 100, Table 2).

All three eligibility criteria are supported, and has_randomized_people_study is true. The short form's core = unclear is its prescribed referral status, and the unfilled fields were intentionally left at defaults under that brief; these are not source disagreements (PDF p. 4, printed p. 98, sections 3.1-3.3; codex-jobs/lscreen-c696/brief.md, SHORT form and eligibility instructions).
This is an original experiment, not a synthesis, so synthesis study counts, pooled estimates, intervals and standardizers are inapplicable (PDF pp. 4-6, printed pp. 98-100, sections 3-4).
summary: The paper reports an online randomized GPT-4o coaching versus web-search experiment with 300 analyzed people and output-scored creativity, so it belongs in the two-screener pipeline. Counts and numerical findings match the PDF, including the acknowledged reversal of adjusted condition labels in Table 2; the only correction is corrupted statistical notation and range/locator characters.
